advanced.summary: Advanced Git is about tools for finding regressions, juggling several checkouts, composing repositories, handling large files, automating with hooks and plumbing, and knowing which of these are local conveniences versus enforceable controls.
points: `git bisect` binary-searches history; `bisect run` uses exit codes: 0 good, 125 skip, 1–127 bad, ≥128 aborts.
Worktrees share objects and refs but each has its own HEAD, index and files; a branch can be checked out in only one worktree.
Submodules are gitlinks (mode 160000) pinning a commit; clone with `--recurse-submodules` or run `git submodule update --init --recursive`.
Git LFS stores ~130-byte pointers in history; without LFS installed (or `lfs: true` in CI) you get the pointer text instead of the file.
Hooks are never cloned; share them via `core.hooksPath` or a hook manager, and enforce policy server-side or in CI because `--no-verify` skips client hooks.
Scripts should use plumbing and porcelain modes: `status --porcelain`, `rev-parse --verify --quiet`, `for-each-ref`, and exit codes like `diff --quiet`.
For huge repos: partial clone (`--filter=blob:none`), cone-mode sparse checkout, and `git maintenance` keep things fast without losing history.
traps: Setting `core.hooksPath` makes Git ignore everything still in `.git/hooks/`.
Commits made inside a submodule on a detached HEAD become unreachable after the next `submodule update`.
`git lfs track` doesn't shrink existing history; only `git lfs migrate import` (a history rewrite) does.
